course_name_en: KMM4622 — Process Design in Chemical Engineering 2

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to use mathematics, basic science, and engineering knowledge learned previously in chemical engineering education to perform any process design.

Ability to perform economic analysis and cost estimation of a plant, process, and equipment, compare different processes and equipment with profitability analysis, and optimize heat exchanger networks.
Ability to research necessary resources and use modern information tools for the design of a process and equipment.
Ability to work individually and in groups.
Ability to prepare technical reports, communicate in written and oral forms, and develop oneself by following advancements in science and technology.

syllabus_topics: Engineering Economic Analysis - Economic Analysis of Chemical Processes: Capital Cost Estimation, Production Cost Estimation, Profitability Analysis
Process Optimization - Optimization of Chemical Processes: Topological Optimization, Parametric Optimization, Optimization of Heat Exchanger Networks
Important Considerations for Plant Location for Chemical Plants: Site Selection, Plant Layout, Environmental Impact Analysis, Safety and Health Factors
Computer-Aided Design Project Work - Written and Oral Presentation of the Report

Peters, M.S., Timmerhaus, K.D., Plant Design and Economics for Chemical Engineers, 4th Ed., McGraw-Hill Book Company, Inc., Singapore, 1991.
Silla, H., Chemical Process Engineering Design and Economics, Marcel Dekker, Inc. New Jersey, 2003.
